chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Women pianists in Kansas City
summary: She says other women played like men, among them Julia Lee, but she was unique in an all-male band, and afterwards some bands in St. Louis hired girls.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: You mentioned other women. Who were some of the other women?
Julia Lee was a great pianist - oh, goodness, I can't remember. It's been so long. But they played like men.
But in other words, you were not particularly unique in Kansas City?
No, just unique being with the band, all male band.
The others were playing by themselves?
Wasn't Julia Lee playing with her brother's band?
Oh, yes, but I was somebody that started that. After I did that several bands got girls in St. Louis.
It was just like Count Basie started the beat that he had, then everybody else came in with the idea.
